newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HIKES FUEL, ENERGY PRICES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HIKES FUEL, ENERGY PRICES.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday raised petrol, diesel and electricity prices by up to 18 percent at its monthly review, in line with inflation and a fall in the national currency, a government official said.

"Petrol prices will rise by an average of 18 percent and diesel fuel prices by 14 percent, effective from Friday," National Price Commission chairman Dimitar Grivekov told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting.
Electricity and coal prices will go up by an average of 9.7 percent.
The government revises energy prices each month, taking account of inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.

The government decided to keep unchanged the prices of central heating and low-grade coal during winter months after thousands of Bulgarians gave up central heating at their homes due to unaffordably high prices.
The price rise brings petrol prices to 129-170 levs ($0.47-$0.63) per litre, diesel fuel prices to 103 levs per litre ($0.38) while electricity prices neared 7 levs per kilowatthour or around $0.03.
Energy prices have risen 326 percent for the first 10 months of 1996, official statistics showed.
Inflation for October was 17.6 percent while cumulative inflation for the first 10 months was 195 percent.
The Bulgarian lev fell from 70 to the dollar at the beginning of the year to 270 on Thursday.

Bulgaria imports more than 80 percent of raw materials for its energy sector and pays for the supplies after it exchanges levs for dollars. The prices of electricity, coal and heating include value added tax of 22 percent.
